_readme: THE ACT REGISTRY (DRE-2825). One file, read by everything.
An ACT is something the pipeline does on its own and then announces: a
refusal, a recovery, or a hold. Until this file existed every act
announced itself in prose and every reader scraped that prose
independently — ten tag constants scattered through scripts/reconcile.py,
the console pattern-matching separate string markers, a sweep deciding
'was that the bot' from an emoji prefix. The vocabulary was remembered in
six places instead of declared in one.
Per act: the TAG it is keyed on, its KIND, the STATE it leaves the work
in, the NEXT ACTOR, what it DISCHARGES, and its SUBSCRIBER — the workflow
expected to act on it.
THE TRAILER IS ADDITIVE. THIS IS THE PART TO GET RIGHT.
The tags below are not prose. They are IDEMPOTENCY KEYS and PER-SHA
BUDGET COUNTERS: reconcile suppresses a repeat notice with `tag in body`,
and _worker_receipt_count enforces CRASHED_REVIEW_RETRY_CAP and
DEPENDABOT_RECEIPT_CAP by counting the receipts that carry one. Change the
grammar and every in-flight pull request's existing receipts become
invisible: budgets re-arm from zero and suppressed comments re-post. So
this file ADOPTS those tags as data — `adopted: true` — and
pipeline_act.receipt() reproduces the existing body BYTE-IDENTICALLY,
appending a trailer and nothing else. No constant is deleted, and
reconcile._AGENT_COMMENT_PREFIXES in particular stays until every
commenter emits a trailer; its removal is a separate, later card.
`adopted: false` means the act has a live receipt but no idempotency key
yet, so its tag is declared here and emitted by a later card. The check
proves such a tag is genuinely absent from the tree — the registry cannot
quietly claim an emission it does not have.
NAMES ARE NOT TAGS, and that is load-bearing. A trailer carries its own
act's name and the name of whatever it discharges; if a name contained
another act's tag, an idempotency check keyed on that tag would read this
receipt as the other act's and suppress it forever — the additive trailer
would stop being additive. problems() refuses it.
SUBSCRIBER IS DECLARED HERE AND RESOLVED ELSEWHERE. Asserting that every
subscriber names a workflow that exists and accepts that trigger is
DRE-2827, and it has to be an extension of the shipped
scripts/check_workflow_watchers.py: `workflow_call` reusables run under
the CALLER's workflow name, and most bureau-pipeline workflows are
reusables. A second, independent derivation of the same fact beside the
shipped one is the hazard this epic exists for.
JSON, not YAML: scripts/reconcile.py imports the reader on every product
repo's sweep, where there is no pip install and PyYAML is not guaranteed.
THE `unconverted` BLOCK (DRE-2826). Emission is enforced by
scripts/check_act_receipts.py: every `gh pr comment`, `gh issue comment`
and `_post_pr_note` call in scripts/ and .github/workflows/ either composes
its body through pipeline_act.receipt() or is named below, with the reason
it does not. Nothing else passes, so a recovery added in a hurry fails CI
instead of posting a receipt nothing downstream can read.
The block is the record of the debt, not a mute button. A row must match
EXACTLY ONE receipt site (a row matching none has outlived the site it
excused; one matching two is excusing a site nobody chose), must carry a
reason, and must disappear the moment that site starts composing. Two
kinds: `not-an-act` — a verdict or a report, which creates no obligation
and hands the work to nobody, so a trailer would answer questions it was
never asked; `undeclared-act` — act-shaped, with no row in `acts` above.
Every `undeclared-act` row is a candidate for the registry, and giving it
one is a registry change rather than an emission change.
Check this file against the code that emits it:
python3 scripts/pipeline_act.py check
What the act IS, in three words the whole pipeline can share. The kind
is not severity: a hold can be routine and a refusal can be trivial.
kinds.refusal: The pipeline declined to act, and says why. The work stays exactly where it was.
kinds.recovery: The pipeline acted to move the work on by itself — a dispatch, a re-dispatch, a restart.
kinds.hold: The pipeline stopped and handed the work to a person. Nothing else is coming until they act.

_readme: The state the act leaves the WORK in — the card or the pull request —
never the state of the run that took the act. A reader asks 'what is
true now', and these are the only four answers.
states.unchanged: Nothing moved. The notice is the whole act, and it is on the record.
states.held: Stopped and labelled for a person; no run will be dispatched at it.
states.escalated: Moved into a human queue lane — the work is now somebody's to answer.
states.dispatched: A run has been dispatched and is expected to report back.

acts.name: blocker-reference-broken
acts.means: A blocker reference on the card does not resolve in Linear, so the dependency gate cannot evaluate it.
acts.why: One bad reference used to kill the WHOLE sweep (DRE-2035). The gate now skips just the unevaluable card and says so once; the rest of the fleet is unaffected. Nothing is repaired here, which is why this is a refusal and not a hold: the card is not stopped, it is merely not read.

emits.anchor: a blocker reference on this card doesn't

acts.name: card-stranded
acts.means: A card sits in an active lane with no evidence any run ever started — no route, no run receipt, or nothing at all recorded in Planning.
acts.why: The board said work was happening while nothing ran; DRE-1978 sat in Planning for seven days and the CEO found it by asking. One tag covers the three conditions that all mean the same thing to a reader — no run has begun — because it is one idempotency key and splitting it would let the same card be flagged three times.

acts.name: intake-overdue
acts.means: A card has sat in Intake past the window the lane contract gives it with nothing happening to it, and has been moved into the CEO's queue.
acts.why: A move rather than a report, on purpose: about 480 consecutive green sweeps once printed, in plain English, the exact reason five cards were frozen, and nobody read one. A report is a record; a move is a gate (DRE-2687).

acts.name: pr-without-checks
acts.means: An open pull request has had zero completed check runs on its head commit — no CI, no verdict and no merge gate will ever fire on it.
acts.why: A conflicted or event-starved pull request is invisible to every other backstop: nothing is red, so nothing alarms. The notice names whether the card is human-parked, because that changes entirely what the reader should do about it.

emits.anchor: pipeline cannot see it: no CI, no critic verdict, no merge

acts.name: work-never-landed
acts.means: Work exists that no pull request has ever been opened for — a branch ahead of the default with no PR, or a hand-built card with neither.
acts.why: CI, the critic, the merge gate and the Linear sync all key off a pull request; a branch on its own passes through no gate at all and closes no card. Keyed on the branch rather than the card, so a second branch that strands the same way still speaks.

emits.anchor: and no pull request has ever been opened for it

acts.name: fix-loop-restarted
acts.means: An operator decision landed after the fix agent's last blocker, so the sweep re-dispatched the fix agent — no hand dispatch needed.
acts.why: The one act in this file that answers another: the fix agent's blocker notice put the work in a human's queue, and this is what takes it back out (DRE-2409). One restart per answer; a further decision comment re-arms it.

emits.anchor: an operator decision landed after the

acts.name: dependabot-review-forced
acts.means: A dependabot pull request cannot review itself — its runs get GitHub's empty Dependabot secrets store — so the sweep dispatched the critic instead.
acts.why: DRE-2047 at the vendor boundary: `secrets: inherit` passes nothing from the Dependabot store, so the token mint died at required-secret validation with zero steps. The receipt is bound to the head sha and CAPPED per sha (DEPENDABOT_RECEIPT_CAP) — which is exactly why its tag may never be reworded.

emits.anchor: pull_request runs get GitHub's empty Dependabot secrets store

acts.name: review-retried-after-crash
acts.means: The review run for this head crashed without producing a verdict — an infra failure, not a code rejection — so the sweep re-dispatched it.
acts.why: DRE-2282. At most CRASHED_REVIEW_RETRY_CAP automatic re-dispatch per head sha; a new commit re-arms a fresh budget. The count lives in the sha-bound receipts, so repeated sweeps cannot spend it twice — the tag IS the counter.

emits.anchor: run for this head crashed (an infra failure

acts.name: reviewer-unavailable
acts.means: The adversarial reviewer is down: its run crashed on this commit and the sweep's automatic re-dispatches crashed too.
acts.why: Past the retry cap the stall is reported rather than retried — a bounded vendor-boundary retry, the DRE-1921 lesson. It discharges the re-dispatch: the obligation that act created was 'a verdict will post', and this is the other way that obligation ends.

emits.anchor: the adversarial reviewer is DOWN for open PR

acts.name: verdict-left-behind
acts.means: A pull request's newest verdict binds an older commit than its head, and no review is running or queued.
acts.why: The merge gate rightly ignores a stale verdict (DRE-1990), so nothing is red and nothing re-reviews on its own — PR #128 carried an APPROVE two commits behind its head through the 2026-08-07 outage. The tenth reconcile tag; the card that opened this registry counted nine.

emits.anchor: has its newest review verdict bound to

acts.name: conflict-agent-dispatched
acts.means: A pull request went DIRTY, so the conflict sweep dispatched the fix agent in conflict mode to merge the default branch into it.
acts.why: A conflicted pull request emits no workflow events at all — GitHub cannot build a merge commit, so no CI runs and the merge gate's DIRTY path never fires (PR #25 sat 17 minutes for a hand-nudge). The receipt is the dispatch announcement the fix run posts; it carries no idempotency key today, because the busy-guard rather than a marker is what bounds it.

emits.anchor: 🔀 Conflict-resolution agent dispatched (round ${{ steps.pr.outputs.attempt }}/5) — merging main into PR #${{ steps.pr.outputs.number }}.

acts.name: fix-attempt-landed
acts.means: The fix agent pushed a new commit, so CI and the critic review re-run on it.
acts.why: Only a NEW commit re-triggers CI and the critic; the workflow verifies the head sha actually advanced before saying this, because announcing 'review re-running' when it did not is a lie that stalls the card in the review lane (DeltaSolv PR #74).

emits.anchor: 🔧 Fix attempt ${{ steps.pr.outputs.attempt }} pushed — CI and critic review re-running.

acts.name: fix-attempt-disputed
acts.means: The fix agent hit a blocker — it disagrees with the reviewer's blocking finding and stopped rather than force a change it believes is wrong.
acts.why: The fixer pushed nothing, so the branch holds a stale REQUEST_CHANGES the critic will never lift on its own. The card is parked for a human rather than left to stall invisibly in the review lane. Its answer is picked up by the sweep and discharged by `fix-loop-restarted`.

acts.name: run-failure-diagnosed
acts.means: A workflow failed twice — the original run and one automatic retry — so the medic diagnosed it in plain English on the card.
acts.why: Not a transient flake by the time it gets here: the retry already happened, and on a critic infra-crash or an upstream 5xx the medic deliberately neither retries nor diagnoses, because re-running against an exhausted limit cannot succeed and only deepens it (DRE-1921). The body is written by the diagnosis agent, so the anchor pins the WRITE CALL rather than any wording.

emits.note: The medic's report is agent-authored prose, so there is no fixed wording to pin. The anchor is the write call in the medic's own prompt — the point at which the receipt is emitted.

unconverted.means: The fix loop refuses to dispatch another identical run at a commit two runs already ended with nothing to show.
unconverted.why: Act-shaped, and the registry has no row for it. DRE-2825 declared thirteen acts by reading reconcile.py's ten tag constants, the fix loop's three notices and the medic; this receipt was not among them. Giving it a row is a REGISTRY change — a tag, a kind, a state, a next actor, a subscriber, and the reasoning that fixes each — not an emission change, and this card converts what the registry declares. Named here so the debt is countable rather than invisible. It already carries its own idempotency key (fix-convergence-halt @<sha8>), read back by this same workflow.

unconverted.means: The adversarial critic's verdict on the pull request.
unconverted.why: A VERDICT, not an act. It is a judgement about the WORK, where an act is something the pipeline did about the work on its own. It is also an approval credential — the merge gate reads it, and standards/untrusted-content.md forbids anything but the critic emitting verdict-shaped text — so a second grammar inside it is a hazard, not an improvement.

unconverted.means: The independent verifier's PASS/FAIL on the pull request.
unconverted.why: A VERDICT, not an act — the same reasoning as the critic's above, and the merge gate reads this one too.
